facts.fact: Medica Magazine reports the Algerian hospital system is now interconnected with the Interior Ministry's civil-status database, allowing instant identification of a patient by biometric card.

systems.system: Hospital link to Interior Ministry civil-status database

DZA.note: No civil register to ID exchange of births or deaths stated.
Civil registration of births and deaths is not described.

facts.fact: The Health Ministry's director general of information systems says the ministry will launch national generalisation of the electronic medical record in summer 2026, and the minister follows each phase personally.

The article says a single national medical record is created automatically around the national identifier and health professionals can consult it from any health institution in the country, with the rollout still to be generalised in summer 2026.

DZA.note: No count or share of people holding the ID is given.
Nothing on a number given at birth.
Nothing on who operates, maintains or owns the ID system.

facts.fact: The Health Ministry says the national electronic medical record, to be generalised in summer 2026, is created around each person's national identifier.
The article describes patients identified instantly through their biometric card against the Interior Ministry's civil-status database, with a national identifier.
facts.system: biometric national card and national identifier

facts.fact: Medica Magazine reports hospitals are connected to the Interior Ministry's civil-status database, from which patients are identified by their biometric card.

DZA.note: No registry office entry of births or deaths stated.
